messages:
maria: Quick proposal — can we standardize span names for LLM requests to be compact and easy to parse? Draft below.
```
span.name: "llm.op"
span.attributes:
  llm.model: "gpt-j-16"
  llm.model_version: "v1.3"
  llm.op_type: "generate|embed|rerank"
  llm.tokens.prompt: 120
  llm.tokens.completion: 45
  llm.cache.hit: true
  llm.batch.size: 8
  llm.stream: false
```
I think keeping the name generic (llm.op) and pushing specifics into attrs will make routing/aggregation easier. Thoughts?

kevin: +1 for compact naming. question: streaming vs non-streaming — do we use a single span with events for chunks or separate spans per chunk?

maria: single span + events for chunk boundaries. per-chunk spans blow up traces and make sampling messy. events can carry chunk_size and seq_no.

andre: agree with single span. also security/retention guardrail: don't include prompt text or long prompt hashes as attributes. token counts OK but redact any prompt content.

lisa: prefer \`llm.op\` as name too but would shorten attribute keys: e.g., \`llm.m\` for model? downside: harder to read. maybe keep readability for ops. also suggest adding \`llm.variant\` to indicate quantized/float32/float16.

telemetry-bot: heads up: current OTLP exporter (otlp-prod) truncates attribute values >255 chars. keys are fine but watch long model strings from vendor metadata.

kevin: +1 on \`llm.variant\`. proposal: standardize on \`llm.model\` and \`llm.model_version\` (explicit) to avoid key collisions with external tooling.

maria: updated concise proposal:
- span.name = "llm.op"
- attributes (required): 
  - "llm.model" (string)
  - "llm.model_version" (string)
  - "llm.op_type" (enum: generate, embed, rerank)
  - "llm.tokens.prompt" (int)
  - "llm.tokens.completion" (int)
  - "llm.cache.hits" (int) or boolean? prefer int for hit count
  - "llm.batch.size" (int)
  - "llm.variant" (string: "quantized"/"fp32"/"fp16")
  - "llm.stream" (bool)
- events for streaming chunks: event.name = "llm.chunk" with attrs: "seq_no", "chunk_tokens"
- do NOT attach prompt text; include "eval_id" or "trace_prompt_hash" (short, <=64 chars) if needed for debug

andre: LGTM. also suggest an attribute for routing decisions: "llm.route_reason" (e.g., "latency_slo"/"cost_pref") so we can later filter traces by fallback routing.

lisa: can product/security review retention/export policy? if we keep token counts and model ids, default retention 30d for detailed spans and 90d for aggregates might be ok. I'll raise with security. :shield:

maria: great. i'll draft a short RFC with these fields and include examples of OTLP JSON and the proposed dashboard groupings (by model, op_type, cache hit rate, batch size). linking it back here when ready. :spiral_note_pad:

kevin: one more: add "llm.kv_cache_hits" (int) vs "llm.cache.hits" to disambiguate. small bikeshed but useful for queries.

maria: good point — will include both names in RFC as alias mapping. thanks everyone.
